Do Internet mods realize just how small and insignificant the power they wield is?
I dunno, I've got an effective monopoly on the dice here.

To me, moderating for a community isn't about how much you matter to the world, but about how much your interactions matter to each individual. You may not exercise any authority across the internet, but being respectful and helpful on a case-by-case basis can make a world of difference to someone. It also reflects well on the community you work for and the site as a whole.

This is an extremely important point.

You do not have to be able to crush a legion in order to change the world for a single person. And in some cases, a few words on the Internet - or in the world at large, even - can mean the difference between life and death.

Exactly. A comment doesn't have to make waves to reach just one person in a powerful way, so all the more reason to treat every interaction like it matters. Oftentimes people understand that moderators specifically have to make tough calls at times, but no one appreciates a moderator who has a snide attitude or belittles people. Even standing your ground on an issue is something that can be done respectfully.

I'm actually rather glad that there are other people who understand this. To be honest, there were times where it felt like I was the only one.

When I was a moderator (of sorts, only slightly similar to such a responsibility at Voat, long story), I HATED making calls against people, especially when I knew it'd hurt them, or crap on something they'd worked on a lot or invested in heavily, or otherwise did damage. In fact, I was too darn soft way too often. But, sometimes, it had to be done. You also have to realize that people are going to be scared of you, and your words often carry weight simply by the tag you're carrying. Sometimes you CAN'T participate in a conversation just like anyone else for that very reason.

Note that I am not discounting that there are shitty moderators out there. A lot of them. And they tend to abuse their power greatly. But there are good ones too, and the responsibility when doing the job well can be a seriously double-edged sword. While I did not seek moderator power like many do, before I had it, at times I rather envied their apparent abilities. Suffice it to say that it is not always evident what comes with those abilities, at least if you're going to try to do a good job with them. It's one reason why I say being a good mod can be a serious skill.

I took pride in keeping things running, but ultimately there are a number of reasons I don't do this sort of thing anymore - not the least of which being, I'm too darn nice for it.

I think that's a good perspective. Having a moderating role is more responsibility than power, but not everyone realizes that. If you try to exercise your role for power's sake, you end up losing both. Whenever it seems like there are too few responsible people out there, I just take solace in the fact that bad mods may get all the attention while good mods often don't need that attention. That means there's more good out there than you might realize when you're having a bad day.
